disease_label_per_paper: Right acute pyelonephritis complicated with sepsis-induced DIC and later renal artery thrombosis
presentation_summary: 65-year-old woman with 20-year diabetes presented to the emergency room with right flank pain and fever.
Physical examination showed BP 80/50 mmHg, temperature 39 C, pulse 130/min, respiratory rate 20/min, and right flank knocking tenderness.

Initial labs: WBC 23,400/uL, hemoglobin 9.7 g/dL, platelets 97,000/uL, CRP 21.97 mg/dL, BUN 35.3 mg/dL, creatinine 2.21 mg/dL, sodium 142 mEq/L, potassium 3.7 mEq/L, albumin 2.4 g/dL, INR 1.63, aPTT 52.8 s, fibrinogen 429.3 mg/dL.
Urinalysis showed trace protein, 10-19 WBC/HPF and 0-1 RBC/HPF.
Initial contrast CT showed a focal wedge-shaped perfusion defect in the upper pole of the right kidney consistent with acute pyelonephritis, with no renal arterial filling defect initially.

E. coli was isolated from both blood and urine cultures; she received IV ceftriaxone, later piperacillin-tazobactam during septic shock; flank pain recurred with renal artery thrombosis during recovery.

risk_context.source_text_value: diabetes for 20 years on oral hypoglycemic agents
